project.name: spo-property-portal
project.description: A property management portal for Saint Paul's Outreach, Inc. (SPO), where staff manage properties, maintenance requests, walkthrough inspections, physical assets, vendor contacts and invoices, and residents submit and track their own maintenance requests. It is a single Express server on Node 20 that serves both the REST API and the React SPA on one port, backed by PostgreSQL through Drizzle ORM. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: uploadLimits.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for upload size limits plus guardedUpload, which reserves in-flight byte capacity from Content-Length before the body is read and turns multer's own errors into clear 413/503 answers.
nodes.languageNotes: Capacity is reserved before parsing and released when the response finishes or the client disconnects, so a burst of large uploads degrades into retries rather than an out-of-memory crash.

nodes.name: readConfiguredCeiling
nodes.summary: Reads and validates MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES_IN_FLIGHT, falling back to the 64MB default when it is absent or unusable.

nodes.name: currentInFlightUploadBytes
nodes.summary: Reports the bytes currently reserved by in-flight uploads, exposed for tests and diagnostics.

nodes.name: maxInFlightUploadBytes
nodes.summary: Reports the configured in-flight upload ceiling.

nodes.name: reserveUploadCapacity
nodes.summary: Reserves capacity from the request's Content-Length before the body is read and releases it when the response finishes or the client disconnects, answering 503 with Retry-After when the ceiling would be exceeded.

nodes.name: withUploadErrorHandling
nodes.summary: Handles multer's own errors locally so an oversized file returns 413 stating the limit rather than the generic message the final error handler would produce.

nodes.name: guardedUpload
nodes.summary: Composes the capacity reservation, the multer middleware and the local error handling into the middleware chain every upload route must use.

nodes.name: ownership.test.ts
nodes.summary: Route-level tests for the resident ownership gate on maintenance requests, confirming the check compares the stored `submittedBy` email against the signed-in user's email.

nodes.name: region.test.ts
nodes.summary: Small unit suite for region name normalisation, guarding the kebab-case versus Title Case format mismatch that once made stored regions fail to match a user's allowedRegions.

nodes.name: routeAccess.test.ts
nodes.summary: The largest suite: end-to-end access-control tests over real HTTP with the real isAuthenticated guard, real authz helpers and real route handlers, replacing only the database and the file store.
nodes.languageNotes: Only the Passport session object is simulated; everything downstream is production code, so removing a guard from a route or reordering checks after the work fails here.

nodes.name: schedules.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the preventive and safety schedule engine: generation fires once per due cycle rather than spamming a fresh request daily for the same overdue task, and safety tasks come through as safety work.

nodes.name: uploadAccess.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests who may download an uploaded file — W-9s, certificates of insurance, contract invoices and photos of people's homes — by exercising canReadUpload against stubbed upload references.

nodes.name: getJson
nodes.summary: Test helper issuing a GET against the live test server and returning status plus parsed JSON body for the ownership assertions.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Test helper performing an authenticated HTTP call against the real Express app with a simulated Passport session, returning status and body for the access-control assertions.

nodes.name: schedule
nodes.summary: Test helper producing a MaintenanceSchedule fixture with sensible defaults so each case only states the due date, interval or category it cares about.

nodes.name: context
nodes.summary: Test helper assembling the AuthContext used by the upload-access cases, varying role, active state, permissions and regions.

nodes.name: uploadRow
nodes.summary: Test helper producing an uploads table row fixture with a storage key and uploader, standing in for a stored file.

nodes.name: seed-demo-data.ts
nodes.summary: Standalone seeding script that fills an empty database with realistic demo properties, residents, maintenance work and vendor records, writing everything through the real storage layer and refusing to run if any properties already exist.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs as a one-shot Node process: it drives the same `storage` singleton the routes use, then calls `closeDatabase()` so the pool does not keep the process alive.

nodes.name: audit.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the audit helper, pinning the two properties that make it safe: it never records a credential (scrubDetails redaction) and it never fails the request it is recording.

nodes.name: authz.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the authorization rules in server/authz.ts, calling the real helpers rather than a copy so region and permission logic cannot drift away from what production runs.
nodes.languageNotes: Stubs `../db` and `../auth` with `vi.mock` so importing authz.ts does not open a database connection — the suite is pure logic and runs in milliseconds.

nodes.name: errors.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the error classification and Express error middleware: every failing request gets a sensible status and a message safe to show, and never hangs or takes the process down.

nodes.name: jotformWebhook.test.ts
nodes.summary: Route-level tests driving the real JotForm webhook over HTTP with both JSON and multipart encodings, asserting on the maintenance request actually stored rather than just the status code.

nodes.name: seedImage
nodes.summary: Stores a 1x1 placeholder PNG through the configured file store and creates its uploads row, returning the /uploads URL so seeded image references actually resolve.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: The whole seeding run: refuses to proceed if properties already exist, then creates properties, residents, rent and deposits, maintenance requests and schedules, vendors, invoices and billing through the storage layer.

nodes.name: response
nodes.summary: Test helper building a fake Express Response that records the status and JSON body an authorization helper wrote, so refusals can be asserted precisely.

nodes.name: context
nodes.summary: Test helper assembling an AuthContext with a role, active flag, permission flags and allowed regions, so each case states only what it varies.

nodes.name: audit.ts
nodes.summary: Append-only audit log of access, money and document events, with credential scrubbing, bounded summaries and a daily retention job that keeps routine entries two years and account/permission history indefinitely.
nodes.languageNotes: recordAuditEvent returns immediately and swallows both a synchronous throw and a rejected write, so an unreachable log can never fail the request it is recording.

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: OpenID Connect login through Passport plus the PostgreSQL-backed session store, exposing setupAuth, the isAuthenticated guard and getUserId — the only supported way to learn who is signed in.
nodes.languageNotes: Claim mapping leaves absent fields `undefined` rather than `null`, because Drizzle's conflict-update filters `undefined` out but writes `null` through and would blank stored names.

nodes.name: authz.ts
nodes.summary: The authorization model: loads the auth context, enforces active-user, role and per-feature permission checks with an admin bypass, and scopes every list and record to the caller's allowed regions.
nodes.languageNotes: filterByRegion deliberately returns an empty array for an empty or null allowedRegions — no regions means no access, not all access.

nodes.name: db.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle ORM over a standard pg Pool, resolving SSL and pool size from the environment and exposing pingDatabase and closeDatabase for health checks and graceful shutdown.
nodes.languageNotes: Throws at import time when DATABASE_URL is missing, which is why every unit test mocks `../db` before importing anything that reaches it.

nodes.name: errors.ts
nodes.summary: Error classification and the final Express error middleware: turns Zod, Drizzle and HttpError failures into a status plus a message safe to show, and hides everything else behind a generic message.

nodes.name: scrubDetails
nodes.summary: Redacts any detail whose key name looks like a secret or a banking identifier before it reaches the audit table, as the backstop that keeps one careless call from leaking a token into a never-deleted table.

nodes.name: auditRetentionCutoff
nodes.summary: Computes the two-year cutoff timestamp before which routine audit entries are eligible for deletion.

nodes.name: purgeExpiredAuditEvents
nodes.summary: Deletes routine audit entries older than the retention cutoff in capped batches, deliberately preserving account and permission events indefinitely.

nodes.name: runScheduledAuditCleanup
nodes.summary: Runs one retention pass, looping over capped deletes and logging rather than throwing so a failed cleanup cannot destabilise the server.

nodes.name: startAuditLogRetentionJob
nodes.summary: Starts the once-a-day retention timer, unref'd so it never keeps the process alive on shutdown.

nodes.name: recordAuditEvent
nodes.summary: Records one audit event fire-and-forget: scrubs details, flattens and truncates the summary, and swallows both a synchronous throw and a rejected write so the log can never fail the request it describes.

nodes.name: auditLookup
nodes.summary: Builds the filtered, paginated audit log query behind GET /api/audit-log for the Settings activity trail.

nodes.name: changedFields
nodes.summary: Diffs a before and after record into the list of field names that actually changed, so an update event records what moved rather than the whole body.

nodes.name: getSession
nodes.summary: Builds the Express session middleware backed by connect-pg-simple, with cookie security, TTL and store settings derived from the environment.

nodes.name: getUserId
nodes.summary: The single supported accessor for the signed-in user's ID, throwing when there is no authenticated user so no route ever reads a provider claim directly.

nodes.name: setupAuth
nodes.summary: Wires the whole OpenID Connect flow: session middleware, Passport strategies cached per domain, the login, callback and logout routes, and claim-to-user mapping.

nodes.name: isAuthenticated
nodes.summary: The route guard: requires a Passport session with a subject claim and refreshes an expired token, answering 401 when there is no refresh token to use.

nodes.name: loadAuthContext
nodes.summary: Loads the signed-in user and their permissions row into an AuthContext, computing isAdmin so every downstream check can bypass on it.

nodes.name: requireActiveUser
nodes.summary: First layer of every data route: resolves the auth context and refuses a missing or deactivated account before any work happens.

nodes.name: hasPermission
nodes.summary: Reads one permission flag with the admin bypass applied, so an admin with no permissions row is never locked out.

nodes.name: requirePermission
nodes.summary: Enforces a named permission flag on a route, writing a 403 and returning false when the caller lacks it.

nodes.name: requireStaff
nodes.summary: Refuses residents on staff-only routes, admitting admins and regional administrators.

nodes.name: requireAdmin
nodes.summary: Restricts a route to full admins, used for user management and other account-level actions.

nodes.name: canAccessRegion
nodes.summary: Decides whether a caller's allowed regions cover a given region, comparing in one canonical form so a legacy slug still matches its Title Case name.

nodes.name: requireRegion
nodes.summary: Single-record region check before a create or delete, refusing work on a region the caller cannot reach.

nodes.name: requireRegionMove
nodes.summary: Update-time region check that validates both the existing and the incoming region, so a record cannot be moved into a region the caller cannot reach.

nodes.name: filterByRegion
nodes.summary: Scopes a list to the caller's allowed regions, deliberately returning nothing when no regions are granted — no regions means no access, not all access.

nodes.name: filterByRelatedRegion
nodes.summary: Scopes a list whose region lives on a related parent record, resolving the parent's region before applying the same rule.

nodes.name: ownsRecord
nodes.summary: Resident ownership check comparing a record's submittedBy email against the signed-in user's email.

nodes.name: canReadMaintenanceRequest
nodes.summary: Combines staff region scoping and resident ownership into one decision about reading a maintenance request.

nodes.name: canReadUploadReference
nodes.summary: Decides read access for a stored file from whichever record references it — asset, walkthrough photo, invoice, billing document or maintenance request.

nodes.name: canReadUpload
nodes.summary: Entry point for upload authorization: authorizes against every record referencing the file, falling back to the uploader when the file is not yet attached to anything.

nodes.name: requireMaintenanceRequestAccess
nodes.summary: Route-level wrapper that answers 403 unless the caller may read the given maintenance request.

nodes.name: resolveSsl
nodes.summary: Chooses the TLS settings for the pg pool from the connection string and environment, disabling SSL only for genuine local connections.

nodes.name: resolvePoolSize
nodes.summary: Reads and bounds the connection pool size from the environment, falling back to a safe default for the hosting platform.

nodes.name: closeDatabase
nodes.summary: Ends the pg pool, used by graceful shutdown and by one-shot scripts so the process can exit.

nodes.name: pingDatabase
nodes.summary: Runs a cheap round-trip query with a timeout so the health endpoint can report database reachability without hanging.

nodes.name: HttpError
nodes.summary: Error subclass carrying an explicit HTTP status and a message the app wrote itself, so intentional refusals reach the client verbatim while everything else is genericised.

nodes.name: fromDatabaseError
nodes.summary: Maps recognisable PostgreSQL error codes — unique violation, foreign key violation, invalid input — onto a client-safe status and message.

nodes.name: classifyError
nodes.summary: The core classifier: turns HttpError, Zod issues, multer failures and database errors into a status plus a safe message, defaulting everything unrecognised to a generic 500.

nodes.name: logError
nodes.summary: Writes the server-side detail for a failed request, keeping the full context out of the client response.

nodes.name: sendError
nodes.summary: The convention every route handler ends with: classifies the error, logs it and writes the response with a caller-supplied fallback message.

nodes.name: asyncHandler
nodes.summary: Wraps an async Express handler so a rejected promise reaches the error middleware instead of hanging the request.

nodes.name: apiNotFound
nodes.summary: Terminal handler answering 404 JSON for unmatched /api routes rather than letting them fall through to the SPA.

nodes.name: errorHandler
nodes.summary: The final Express error middleware, guaranteeing every failing request gets an answer and never takes the process down.

nodes.name: health.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the unauthenticated GET /api/health endpoint used by the hosting platform, reporting database reachability without revealing anything about the deployment.

nodes.name: migrateRegions.ts
nodes.summary: Region name normalisation plus one-off backfills that convert legacy kebab-case region slugs to the canonical Title Case form so stored records match users' allowedRegions.

nodes.name: routes.ts
nodes.summary: The whole REST API in one file: roughly 75 Express handlers covering users and permissions, maintenance requests, walkthroughs, assets, residents, rent and deposits, vendors, invoices, billing, properties, uploads and the JotForm webhook.
nodes.languageNotes: Handlers never touch the database directly — every read and write goes through the `storage` singleton, which is what keeps the data layer testable and swappable.

nodes.name: schedules.ts
nodes.summary: Preventive and safety maintenance scheduling: a daily idempotent job turns due recurring schedules into ordinary maintenance requests so scheduled work lands in the queue staff already watch.
nodes.languageNotes: Date arithmetic runs in UTC and clamps month overflow, so adding a month to Jan 31 lands on the last day of February rather than spilling into March.

nodes.name: storage.ts
nodes.summary: The only place in the app that queries the database: a single DatabaseStorage class behind the IStorage interface, exported as the `storage` singleton every route handler goes through.
nodes.languageNotes: upsertUser contains email-based account re-linking, which lets an admin pre-create an account before someone's first login and makes an identity-provider swap survivable.

nodes.name: registerHealthRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers GET /api/health, pinging the database and reporting status without exposing configuration or version detail.

nodes.name: normalizeRegion
nodes.summary: Maps a legacy kebab-case region slug onto its canonical Title Case name, leaving already-canonical names untouched.

nodes.name: normalizeRegions
nodes.summary: Applies normalizeRegion across a list, used to canonicalise a user's allowedRegions array.

nodes.name: backfillBillingRegions
nodes.summary: One-off backfill filling in missing region values on billing records so region scoping can apply to them.

nodes.name: migrateRegionsToTitleCase
nodes.summary: Rewrites stored kebab-case regions across the affected tables to Title Case, closing the format mismatch that made records invisible to their own region.

nodes.name: secretsMatch
nodes.summary: Constant-time comparison of the JotForm webhook secret, so a mismatch cannot be probed by timing.

nodes.name: requireRoomRegion
nodes.summary: Resolves a walkthrough room's property region and enforces the caller's region access before the room or its photos are touched.

nodes.name: resolveContactLink
nodes.summary: Resolves the maintenance request and contact behind a link or unlink call and checks the caller may act on both sides.

nodes.name: registerRoutes
nodes.summary: Registers every API endpoint on the Express app — roughly 75 handlers plus the authenticated upload reader and the JotForm webhook — and returns the HTTP server.

nodes.name: addMonths
nodes.summary: Adds whole months in UTC, clamping day overflow so a monthly schedule starting Jan 31 lands on the last day of February rather than spilling into March.

nodes.name: needsRequest
nodes.summary: Decides whether a schedule is due and has not already had a request generated for this due date, which is what keeps the daily job idempotent.

nodes.name: requestFromSchedule
nodes.summary: Turns a due schedule into the maintenance request payload, carrying the safety or preventive category through so scheduled safety work is visible as such.

nodes.name: generateDueMaintenanceRequests
nodes.summary: Generates requests for every currently due schedule and marks each one generated for its due date.

nodes.name: runScheduledGeneration
nodes.summary: One pass of the daily generation job, logging failures rather than throwing so a bad schedule cannot stop the timer.

nodes.name: startScheduleGenerationJob
nodes.summary: Starts the once-a-day schedule generation timer at server boot.

nodes.name: computeDefaultPermissions
nodes.summary: Derives the default thirteen permission flags for a newly created account from its role, so a new resident or staff member starts with a sensible grant.

nodes.name: DatabaseStorage
nodes.summary: The single implementation of IStorage: roughly 93 methods covering every table, including the email-based account re-linking in upsertUser and the audit log queries. Nothing else in the app issues a database query.

nodes.name: GET /api/auth/user
nodes.summary: Returns the signed-in database user plus their permission flags — deliberately not provider claims — which is what the whole frontend keys its role-based routing on.

nodes.name: GET /api/users
nodes.summary: Lists accounts for user management, restricted to admins.

nodes.name: PATCH /api/users/:id/role
nodes.summary: Changes an account's role and records a permanently retained user.role_changed audit event.

nodes.name: PATCH /api/users/:id/permissions
nodes.summary: Updates the thirteen permission flags and allowedRegions for an account, auditing exactly which fields changed.

nodes.name: POST /api/users
nodes.summary: Pre-creates an account so an admin can grant a role and permissions before that person's first sign-in ever happens.

nodes.name: DELETE /api/users/:id
nodes.summary: Deletes an account, cascading its permissions row and recording a permanently retained audit event.

nodes.name: GET /api/audit-log
nodes.summary: Serves the filtered, paginated activity trail rendered in Settings.

nodes.name: GET /api/maintenance-requests
nodes.summary: Lists maintenance requests, region-scoped for staff and narrowed to their own submissions for residents.

nodes.name: POST /api/maintenance-requests
nodes.summary: Creates a maintenance request, storing the submitter's email in submittedBy — the value the resident ownership gate later compares against.

nodes.name: PATCH /api/maintenance-requests/:id
nodes.summary: Updates a request and audits a status change, checking both the existing and incoming region so a request cannot be moved out of reach.

nodes.name: GET /api/maintenance-requests/:id/contacts
nodes.summary: Lists the vendors linked to a request; one of the two historic authorization gaps, now guarded and covered by tests.

nodes.name: GET /api/assets
nodes.summary: Lists fixed and movable assets, region-scoped for non-admins.

nodes.name: POST /api/upload
nodes.summary: Image upload endpoint: permission check before multer, magic-byte validation, a server-generated storage key, and a returned /uploads URL.

nodes.name: POST /api/upload-doc
nodes.summary: Document upload endpoint for PDFs and Office files up to 20MB, with the same permission-before-parse ordering and magic-byte validation as image upload.

nodes.name: GET /uploads/:filename
nodes.summary: The authenticated file reader: rejects anything that is not a bare storage key, authorizes against the record referencing the file, checks existence only after authorizing, and either redirects to a short-lived signed URL or streams the bytes privately.

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/jotform
nodes.summary: Turns JotForm submissions into maintenance requests, failing closed with 503 when no webhook secret is configured and comparing the secret in constant time.

nodes.name: GET /api/webhooks/jotform/config
nodes.summary: Exposes the current JotForm field mapping to the admin setup dialog.

nodes.name: POST /api/maintenance-schedules/apply-template
nodes.summary: Applies the standard set of preventive and safety schedules to a property in one action.

nodes.name: POST /api/rent-payments/generate
nodes.summary: Generates the month's rent payment rows for active residents, skipping any that already exist.

nodes.name: PATCH /api/invoices/:id
nodes.summary: Updates an invoice's amount, status or dates and records a money-related audit event.

nodes.name: POST /api/billing
nodes.summary: Creates a vendor billing record with its contract, COI and W-9 document URLs, auditing the change.

nodes.name: GET /api/properties
nodes.summary: Lists properties with their computed unique address, region-scoped for non-admins.

nodes.name: format.ts
nodes.summary: Display-formatting helpers used at the render boundary across the app: currency, percentages, dates, date-times, and an em-dash fallback for missing values. Centralises the Intl formatters so every table and card renders the same way.
nodes.languageNotes: formatDate deliberately reads calendar parts out of date-only strings instead of passing them to new Date(), which would parse them as UTC midnight and display the previous day in US timezones.

nodes.name: queryClient.ts
nodes.summary: Configures the shared TanStack Query client and the fetch helpers every page uses: apiRequest() for mutations (throws on non-2xx) and getQueryFn() as the default query function, which derives the URL by joining the query key with "/".
nodes.languageNotes: staleTime is Infinity with refetchOnWindowFocus and retry disabled, so every mutation must invalidate its query keys by hand or the UI shows stale data.

nodes.name: Assets.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for the fixed and movable asset register: lists, filters by region and building, and creates, edits and deletes assets along with their attached photos. Its mutations invalidate the ["/api/assets"] and ["/api/asset-photos"] query keys.

nodes.name: Contacts.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for vendor contacts and their billing records, with region and building filters, create/edit forms and document uploads for contracts, COI and W-9 files. Mutations invalidate the ["/api/contacts"] and ["/api/billing"] query keys.

nodes.name: Finances.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for resident finances: monthly rent payments (including bulk generation for a period) and security deposits with their return status. Mutations against /api/rent-payments and /api/security-deposits invalidate those two query keys.
nodes.languageNotes: Records only amounts, statuses and dates — no banking credentials, per the project rule that raw account details belong with a payment processor.

nodes.name: Maintenance.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page listing and filtering maintenance requests by status, priority, region and building, with a create form and a link into the edit dialog. Filter state lives in the URL via useUrlState, and creating a request invalidates ["/api/maintenance-requests"].

nodes.name: Properties.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for the property register: lists properties and creates, edits and deletes them through a Zod-validated form over the four address parts, region and chapter. All three mutations invalidate ["/api/properties"].

nodes.name: Residents.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for the resident roster: shows who lives in each house with move-in/move-out dates and contact details, filtered by region and building. Create, update and delete mutations all invalidate ["/api/residents"].

nodes.name: Safety.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for preventive and safety maintenance schedules: shows what is due, overdue or upcoming per property, marks a schedule complete, and can apply a standard template to a property. Mutations invalidate ["/api/maintenance-schedules"].

nodes.name: Walkthroughs.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin page for walkthrough inspections: lists inspection rooms per property, creates rooms and photos, and opens the room detail drawer. Mutations invalidate the ["/api/walkthrough-rooms"] and ["/api/walkthrough-photos"] query keys.

nodes.name: formatCurrency
nodes.summary: Formats a string or numeric amount as USD, optionally to whole dollars, returning an em-dash for null or non-finite values.

nodes.name: formatValue
nodes.summary: Returns the trimmed value, or an em-dash when it is null, undefined or blank, so tables never show an empty cell.

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.summary: Formats a date for display, reading date-only strings as calendar parts so they do not shift a day in US timezones, and using local time for full timestamps.

nodes.name: formatDateTime
nodes.summary: Formats a timestamp as a local date plus time for audit and activity views.

nodes.name: formatPercent
nodes.summary: Formats a ratio as a clamped percentage string with configurable decimals and maximum.

nodes.name: apiRequest
nodes.summary: Mutation helper that sends a JSON request with credentials included and throws an Error prefixed with the status code on any non-2xx response.

nodes.name: getQueryFn
nodes.summary: Default query function factory: joins the query key with "/" to build the URL and either returns null or throws on a 401, depending on the configured behaviour.

nodes.name: Assets
nodes.summary: Page component holding the asset list, region/building filters, permission lookup, and the create/update/delete asset and asset-photo mutations.

nodes.name: Contacts
nodes.summary: Page component holding vendor contact and billing state, the create/edit forms, document upload to /api/upload-doc, and the contact and billing mutations.

nodes.name: Finances
nodes.summary: Page component holding rent payment and security deposit state, the period generator, and the six mutations that create, update and delete both record types.

nodes.name: DepositEditDialog
nodes.summary: Local dialog for editing a security deposit’s return status, amount returned, return date and deduction notes via a Zod-validated form.

nodes.name: Maintenance
nodes.summary: Page component holding maintenance request state, URL-backed status/priority/region/building filters, the create form and the JotForm webhook config lookup.

nodes.name: Properties
nodes.summary: Page component holding property list state and the create, update and delete mutations, each invalidating ["/api/properties"].

nodes.name: Residents
nodes.summary: Page component holding resident roster state, region and building filters, and the create, update and delete resident mutations.

nodes.name: Safety
nodes.summary: Page component holding maintenance schedule state, due/overdue grouping, and the create, complete, delete and apply-template mutations.

nodes.name: Walkthroughs
nodes.summary: Page component holding walkthrough room and photo state, the room create form, and the drawer that opens one room for inspection.

nodes.name: BuildingSelector.tsx
nodes.summary: Presentational dropdown that filters a page by property/building, rendering an "All buildings" option plus one item per building passed in via props. Holds no state of its own — selection is controlled by the parent page.

nodes.name: ContactsInvoices.tsx
nodes.summary: Tabbed read-only panel on the Contacts page that shows vendor contacts on one tab and their billing/invoice records on the other, with phone/email links and document links. Purely presentational — data and edit callbacks come from the parent.

nodes.name: MaintenanceEditDialog.tsx
nodes.summary: Modal editor for a maintenance request: edits status, priority, assignment and notes, and links or unlinks vendor contacts on the request. Mutations PATCH /api/maintenance-requests/:id and POST/DELETE the contact links, invalidating the ["/api/maintenance-requests"] and per-request contacts query keys afterwards.

nodes.name: PhotoUpload.tsx
nodes.summary: Reusable drag-and-drop image picker that POSTs the chosen file as multipart form data to /api/upload and hands the returned storage URL back to its parent. Shows a preview of the existing or newly uploaded image and surfaces upload failures through an onError callback.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the raw fetch API rather than apiRequest because the body is FormData, so the JSON content-type header of the shared helper would break the multipart boundary.

nodes.name: RegionSelector.tsx
nodes.summary: Presentational dropdown for filtering a page by SPO region, with the six region ids hard-coded alongside an "All Regions" option. Controlled entirely by the parent page.

nodes.name: RoomDetailDrawer.tsx
nodes.summary: Side drawer for one walkthrough inspection room: shows and edits the room record, lists its photos with condition and notes, and supports adding, annotating and deleting photos. Its four mutations invalidate the ["/api/walkthrough-photos/room", roomId], ["/api/walkthrough-photos"] and ["/api/walkthrough-rooms"] keys.

nodes.name: use-toast.ts
nodes.summary: Headless toast notification store: a module-level reducer plus listener list that drives the shadcn Toaster, exposing the imperative toast() call and the useToast() subscription hook. Caps the visible toasts and schedules removal after dismissal.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a tiny Redux-style store outside React (module-scoped memoryState plus listeners) so toast() can be called from anywhere, including outside a component tree.

nodes.name: use-url-state.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that mirrors a page’s filter/search/tab state into the URL query string via Wouter, so a filtered view can be bookmarked, shared and restored on refresh. Values equal to their default are dropped from the URL and unrelated query parameters are left untouched.

nodes.name: useAuth.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that reads the signed-in user from GET /api/auth/user and derives isAuthenticated / isLoading, treating a 401 as "signed out" rather than an error. Returns the database user plus permissions, never raw identity-provider claims.

nodes.name: authUtils.ts
nodes.summary: Single helper that recognises an unauthorized error by matching the "401: ..." prefix that apiRequest puts on thrown errors. Used to distinguish a signed-out session from a real failure.

nodes.name: BuildingSelector
nodes.summary: React component rendering the building filter Select, mapping the buildings prop to options plus an "All buildings" entry.

nodes.name: ContactsInvoices
nodes.summary: Renders the two-tab contacts/invoices panel, formatting invoice amounts with formatCurrency and falling back to EmptyState when a tab has no records.

nodes.name: MaintenanceEditDialog
nodes.summary: Modal form component holding the request-edit form plus four mutations: PATCH the request, and link/unlink vendor contacts, each invalidating its own query key on success.

nodes.name: PhotoUpload
nodes.summary: Drag-and-drop image picker that validates the selection, POSTs FormData to /api/upload, shows a preview, and reports the returned URL or an error to its parent.

nodes.name: RegionSelector

nodes.summary: Context accessor returning theme, resolvedTheme and setTheme; throws when used outside a ThemeProvider.

nodes.name: objectStorage.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the file storage layer, exercising key generation, key safety, content-type mapping, the local driver against a temp folder, and the Supabase driver's pre-network guards. Runs with no bucket, credentials or network access.
nodes.languageNotes: The Supabase driver is only exercised for checks that happen before any network call, which is what keeps the suite hermetic.

nodes.name: readAll
nodes.summary: Test helper that drains a Readable stream into a single Buffer so stored bytes can be compared exactly.

nodes.name: config.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for every environment variable the server cannot run without, validated once at boot and reported together. Also owns the OIDC identity-provider settings that let the login provider be swapped without touching code.
nodes.languageNotes: Every OIDC default reproduces Replit Auth, so the app keeps working on Replit while OIDC_* variables can repoint it at any other provider.

nodes.name: checkDatabase
nodes.summary: Validates DATABASE_URL presence and shape, appending a human-readable problem string rather than throwing so all configuration faults can be reported together.

nodes.name: checkSessionSecret
nodes.summary: Checks that a session secret is configured and strong enough, so sessions cannot be signed with a weak or missing key in production.

nodes.name: checkAuth
nodes.summary: Validates the OIDC provider settings — issuer URL, client ID, client secret and scopes — reporting each missing or inconsistent value as its own problem.

nodes.name: checkStorage
nodes.summary: Resolves the configured storage driver and, for the Supabase driver, verifies its bucket credentials can be read from the environment before the server starts.

nodes.name: validateConfiguration
nodes.summary: Runs every configuration check and, if any failed, exits with one numbered list of all problems instead of failing on the first missing variable.
nodes.languageNotes: Collecting problems into an array and reporting them together means an operator fixes one deploy's worth of settings in a single pass.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Application entry point: validates configuration before anything else loads, then sets trust proxy, security headers, JSON body parsing that captures rawBody for webhooks, API request logging, graceful shutdown, and listens on PORT.
nodes.languageNotes: `app.set("trust proxy", 1)` trusts exactly one hop, so a client cannot forge the forwarded-for header by adding its own.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Graceful shutdown path shared by SIGTERM/SIGINT and fatal errors: stops accepting connections, lets in-flight requests finish within a 15s grace window, closes the database pool, then exits.
nodes.languageNotes: The forced-exit timer is unref'd and necessary: an idle keep-alive socket would otherwise hold server.close() open until the platform sends SIGKILL.

nodes.name: logger.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal timestamped logging helper, kept in its own module so the production bundle never has to import the Vite dev middleware that once owned it.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Writes a message to stdout prefixed with a local time stamp and a source tag.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Public face of the file storage layer: selects the driver from STORAGE_DRIVER, lazily builds a single FileStore, and re-exports the key helpers plus thin put/exists/remove/stream/sign wrappers that the rest of the server calls.
nodes.languageNotes: The store is created lazily on first use, so importing this module never reaches for credentials at import time.

nodes.name: resolveStorageDriverName
nodes.summary: Reads STORAGE_DRIVER and resolves it to a supported driver name, defaulting to local outside production, refusing to guess in production, and rejecting unrecognised values rather than silently falling back.

nodes.name: createFileStore
nodes.summary: Constructs the concrete FileStore for a driver name — the Supabase bucket driver in production, a local folder driver in development.

nodes.name: fileStore
nodes.summary: Returns the process-wide FileStore singleton, building it on first use from the resolved driver name.

nodes.name: putUpload
nodes.summary: Stores an uploaded file's bytes under a server-generated storage key with its metadata; the single write path every upload route goes through.

nodes.name: uploadExists
nodes.summary: Reports whether a stored object exists, checked only after a download request has been authorized so a refusal cannot confirm which keys are real.

nodes.name: removeUpload
nodes.summary: Deletes a stored object, used mainly to clean up a half-finished upload.

nodes.name: openUploadStream
nodes.summary: Opens a readable stream over a stored object so the authenticated download route can stream bytes when no signed URL is available.

nodes.name: createUploadSignedUrl
nodes.summary: Requests a short-lived signed URL for a stored object, returning null on drivers that cannot sign so the caller streams instead.

nodes.name: local.ts
nodes.summary: Development FileStore driver backed by a folder on disk, creating the root lazily and refusing any key that could resolve outside it.

nodes.name: createLocalFileStore
nodes.summary: Builds a FileStore over a local directory, implementing put, exists, openReadStream and remove, with every path derived through a key-safety check. Reports that it cannot sign URLs so callers fall back to streaming.
nodes.languageNotes: Closure-based object literal rather than a class — the driver's private state is just the resolved root directory.

nodes.name: supabase.ts
nodes.summary: Production FileStore driver over a private Supabase Storage bucket, including the environment reader that names exactly which settings are missing when it cannot be configured.

nodes.name: readSupabaseConfigFromEnv
nodes.summary: Reads the Supabase URL, service-role key and bucket name from the environment, throwing an error that names every missing variable rather than failing on the first one.

nodes.name: createSupabaseFileStore
nodes.summary: Builds a FileStore over a private Supabase bucket implementing put, exists, remove, openReadStream and createSignedUrl, validating every key before any request leaves the process.
nodes.languageNotes: Download responses arrive as a web ReadableStream and are adapted with Readable.fromWeb so callers see a normal Node stream.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the FileStore interface and StoredObjectMetadata shape that both drivers implement, plus the shared key helpers: content-type mapping, random storage-key generation, and key-safety validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Keys are random rather than derived from the uploaded filename, so a shared URL cannot leak a resident's or property's name.

nodes.name: contentTypeFor
nodes.summary: Maps a filename's extension to a content type from the accepted-upload table, falling back to a neutral octet-stream rather than guessing.

nodes.name: generateStorageKey
nodes.summary: Generates a random 16-byte hex storage key keeping only the original extension, so the uploader's filename never becomes part of a URL.

nodes.name: isSafeStorageKey
nodes.summary: Validates that a storage key is a single harmless path segment — no separators, no traversal, no leading dot, no control characters — before it can reach a disk or a bucket.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately accepts more than generateStorageKey produces so files stored before keys were randomised remain readable.

nodes.name: security.ts
nodes.summary: Owns the Helmet security headers including the production Content Security Policy, plus the rate limiters guarding the upload and webhook endpoints.

nodes.name: storageOrigins
nodes.summary: Derives the storage host origins that the CSP must allow, so signed bucket URLs are not blocked when images and documents load.

nodes.name: securityHeaders
nodes.summary: Builds the Helmet middleware applied to every request, with a strict production Content Security Policy relaxed only enough for the Vite dev server in development.

nodes.name: userOrIpKey
nodes.summary: Rate-limit key generator that buckets by signed-in user when available and falls back to a normalised client IP otherwise.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that runs the project's four-command gate — lint, TypeScript check, Vitest, and build — on every push to any branch and on every pull request. Requires no secrets, database, or bucket, so it runs safely on fork pull requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a `concurrency` group keyed on `github.ref` with `cancel-in-progress`, so a newer push supersedes an in-flight run; `npm ci` is chosen over `npm install` so the lockfile is installed exactly and a lockfile/package.json mismatch fails the run.

nodes.name: e2e.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that runs the Playwright end-to-end suite against a real Postgres service container: it installs Chromium, migrates and seeds a throwaway database, runs `npm run test:e2e`, and uploads the Playwright report as an artifact when the run fails.
nodes.languageNotes: A `services.postgres` container with a `pg_isready` health check supplies the database; the job-level `env` block holds only placeholder OIDC settings and a throwaway session secret, because the browser authenticates through a cookie minted by global-setup rather than a real login.

nodes.name: 0000_baseline_current_schema.sql
nodes.summary: Drizzle baseline migration that records the pre-existing production schema: thirteen tables covering sessions, users and permissions, maintenance, walkthroughs, assets, vendors, invoices, billing and properties, plus the foreign keys and the session-expiry index. Applied to a fresh database it recreates the whole portal from scratch; on the legacy database it is recorded as already applied via `db:baseline`.
nodes.languageNotes: Drizzle-generated SQL: statements are separated by `--> statement-breakpoint` markers, all identifiers are double-quoted, and every foreign key is added as a trailing ALTER TABLE rather than inline.

nodes.name: sessions
nodes.summary: Express session store table (`sid`, `sess` jsonb, `expire`) written and read by connect-pg-simple rather than by application code. Paired with the `IDX_session_expire` index so expired sessions can be swept efficiently.

nodes.name: users
nodes.summary: Account table whose `id` is the identity provider's subject claim, with a unique `email` that makes email-based account re-linking possible on a provider swap. Carries `role` (admin / regional_administrator / resident), `is_active`, and the profile fields mapped from OIDC claims.

nodes.name: user_permissions
nodes.summary: One row per user holding the boolean permission flags (view/manage maintenance, walkthroughs, assets, billing, contacts, users, properties) plus the `allowed_regions` text array used for region scoping. `user_id` is unique and cascades on user delete; admins often have no row at all, which is why every permission check needs the admin bypass.

nodes.name: maintenance_requests
nodes.summary: The core workflow table: title, description, category, priority and status for each request, with region and building address for scoping. `submitted_by` stores an email address rather than a user id, which is how resident ownership is matched. The baseline still includes the legacy `monday_item_id` column later dropped by 0002.

nodes.name: walkthrough_rooms
nodes.summary: Inspection room templates ordered by `display_order`, with `required_questions` and a `property_id` that references properties only loosely (no foreign key declared). `building_address` is retained for backward compatibility with records predating property ids.

nodes.name: walkthrough_photos
nodes.summary: Photos attached to an inspection room with condition and free-form notes; `room_id` has a real foreign key to walkthrough_rooms that cascades on delete. The baseline still carries the `question_answers` column that migration 0006 removes.

nodes.name: assets
nodes.summary: Fixed and movable assets with category, age, serial number, purchase price and asset tag, scoped by region and location. `property_id` is a plain column with no foreign key, so an asset row survives the removal of its property record.

nodes.name: asset_photos
nodes.summary: Photos attached to an asset, with caption and uploader. `asset_id` has a foreign key to assets that cascades on delete, so deleting an asset removes its photo rows (though not the stored files themselves).

nodes.name: maintenance_contacts
nodes.summary: Vendor contact records (name, company, service, phone, email) scoped by region and building address. Referenced by invoices, which set null on delete, and by the request_contacts join table, which cascades.

nodes.name: invoices
nodes.summary: Vendor invoices with number, service, amount, status and due/paid dates. Both `contact_id` and `maintenance_request_id` are foreign keys that set null on delete, so an invoice record outlives the vendor or request it was raised against. Stores amounts and dates only, never banking credentials.

nodes.name: billing_records
nodes.summary: Vendor billing rows holding company details, invoice cost, and three document URLs (contract/invoice, certificate of insurance, W-9). `contact_id` is a plain column with no foreign key, so the row is deliberately independent of the contacts table.

nodes.name: properties
nodes.summary: Property records with the four address parts plus a computed, uniquely constrained `address`, region, property manager and unit details. Rooms and assets point at it only loosely; residents and maintenance schedules added later do declare real cascading foreign keys.

nodes.name: request_contacts
nodes.summary: Join table linking vendor contacts to maintenance requests. Both foreign keys cascade on delete, so the link disappears with either side.

nodes.name: 0001_add_uploads_table.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the `uploads` table that gives every stored file a database record, which is what lets `GET /uploads/:filename` authorize a download against the record referencing the file instead of serving the bucket statically.

nodes.name: uploads
nodes.summary: One row per stored file: a server-generated `storage_key` with a unique constraint, the client's original filename, content type, size in bytes and the uploader's user id. `uploaded_by` has no foreign key on purpose, so the record outlives a deleted account.

nodes.name: 0002_drop_monday_item_id.sql
nodes.summary: Single-statement migration dropping the legacy `monday_item_id` column from `maintenance_requests`, removing the last trace of the previous Monday.com-backed workflow.

nodes.name: 0003_add_audit_log.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the append-only `audit_log` table together with its three read indexes (by created_at, by entity, by actor), the storage behind the activity trail in Settings.

nodes.name: audit_log
nodes.summary: Append-only record of access, money and document events: actor id and email stored as plain columns with deliberately no foreign key, plus action, entity type and id, a human-readable summary, and a scrubbed `details` payload. Rows are never updated, and account and permission events are retained indefinitely while routine events age out after two years.
nodes.languageNotes: The actor columns are intentionally denormalized so a deleted user cannot erase or break their own audit trail.

nodes.name: 0004_add_audit_log_filter_indexes.sql
nodes.summary: Adds two btree indexes to `audit_log` supporting the activity trail's filters: a composite (action, created_at) index for filtering by action in time order, and an index on actor_email.

nodes.name: 0005_add_property_chapter.sql
nodes.summary: Single-statement migration adding the nullable `chapter` column to `properties`, free text recording which SPO chapter uses the property.

nodes.name: 0006_drop_question_answers.sql
nodes.summary: Single-statement migration dropping the unused `question_answers` column from `walkthrough_photos`, leaving the free-form `notes` field as the only per-photo commentary.

nodes.name: 0007_add_maintenance_schedules.sql
nodes.summary: Creates `maintenance_schedules` for preventive and safety maintenance, with foreign keys to properties (cascade) and assets (set null), so a recurring schedule follows the property but survives the asset it was attached to.

nodes.name: maintenance_schedules
nodes.summary: Recurring maintenance definitions: interval in months, last completed and next due dates, plus `last_generated_for_due` as the idempotency marker that stops a due schedule from spawning duplicate maintenance requests. Carries region and building address for the usual region scoping, and `is_active` to retire a schedule without deleting its history.

nodes.name: 0008_add_residents.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the `residents` table recording who lives in each house, with a cascading foreign key to properties so a removed property takes its roster with it.

nodes.name: residents
nodes.summary: Resident roster rows: name, email, move-in and move-out dates, and an `is_active` flag so a past resident stays on record. `property_id` cascades on delete, and region plus building address carry the standard region scoping.

nodes.name: 0009_add_resident_finances.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the two resident finance tables, `rent_payments` and `security_deposits`, both cascading from residents, plus unique indexes enforcing one payment row per resident per period and one deposit row per resident.
nodes.languageNotes: Both tables record only amounts, statuses, dates and a free-text `reference` — no account, routing or card numbers — which is the schema-level expression of the project's rule that raw banking credentials never enter this database.

nodes.name: rent_payments
nodes.summary: Monthly rent rows keyed by resident and `period`, with amount, status, paid date, an external processor `reference` and notes. A unique index on (resident_id, period) makes double-recording a month impossible; `resident_id` cascades on delete.

nodes.name: security_deposits
nodes.summary: One security deposit per resident, enforced by a unique index on `resident_id`: amount held, status, amount returned, return date and deduction notes. Cascades when the resident row is deleted.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Placeholder-only template listing every environment variable the server reads — database URL and pool/SSL settings, session secret, OIDC provider settings, storage driver and Supabase bucket credentials, upload byte ceiling, and the full JotForm field-mapping and default-value set.
nodes.languageNotes: The app deliberately has no dotenv dependency, so this file is documentation for the host's environment rather than something the process loads. It carries placeholders only — no real credentials.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Standing engineering context for the repository: backend and frontend architecture file-by-file, the fifteen-table data model and schema-change procedure, the three-layer authorization model with its admin bypass and region scoping, login, file uploads, the audit log, and a set of permanent rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Encodes a permanent financial-data rule: the portal must never store raw bank, routing, card or ACH credentials — those belong with a processor such as QuickBooks or Stripe, and only references, statuses, dates and amounts may be persisted.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: The project's front door: who uses the portal (admin, regional administrator, resident), the tech stack, how to run it from a fresh clone, the four-command pre-push gate, the project layout, the security and audit model, and deployment notes.

nodes.name: components.json
nodes.summary: shadcn/ui generator configuration pinning the new-york style with TSX and no RSC, and pointing the CLI at the Tailwind config, the theme stylesheet, and the @/ path aliases for components, hooks, lib and utils.

nodes.name: design_guidelines.md
nodes.summary: Portal-specific design rules layered on top of the shared SPO Design System: outlined red CTAs, navy body text, bordered cards, 12px corners, generous section spacing, plus the deviations this app takes and a map of where each design piece lives.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Node package manifest defining the four-command quality gate (lint, check, test, build), the dev/start and Drizzle migration scripts, and the full dependency set for the Express + React single-port application.
nodes.languageNotes: The overrides block is load-bearing: it pins the transitive @esbuild-kit/core-utils esbuild to a patched ^0.25.0 so npm audit stays clean, and should only be removed once drizzle-kit drops the deprecated declaration.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Single strict TypeScript configuration covering client, server and shared code at once, with noEmit type-checking only, bundler module resolution, and the @/ and @shared/ path aliases both halves of the app rely on.
nodes.languageNotes: One tsconfig spans client/src, shared and server, which is what lets shared/schema.ts act as a single source of truth for types on both sides of the wire.

nodes.name: ONBOARDING_AUDIT.md
nodes.summary: Read-only audit of commit d585158 that verifies whether the portal actually builds, type-checks and tests cleanly, inventories every environment variable and Replit branch point needed to run outside Replit, and lists documentation-versus-code discrepancies, delete candidates and the shortest path to a working app. Records the fresh-clone test failure (server/migrateRegions.ts importing server/db.ts at module scope) as a bug rather than fixing it.
nodes.languageNotes: Evidence-driven audit style: every claim is anchored to a file:line citation, and tables carry an explicit confidence column so the reader can judge each finding independently.

nodes.name: PRODUCTION_MIGRATION.md
nodes.summary: Eleven-step runbook for moving the SPO Admin Portal off Replit onto permanent infrastructure — Supabase for Postgres and the private uploads bucket, Google Workspace OpenID Connect for login, and Render for hosting — with a mandatory staging pass, the full Render environment-variable list, deliberate (non-startup) migration application, and a cutover and rollback plan.
nodes.languageNotes: Written as an ordered runbook for a non-developer operator: each step states the settings to enter, why the choice matters (pooled versus direct connection strings, per-environment session secrets), and how to prove it worked before continuing.

nodes.name: spo-design-system.md
nodes.summary: Portable UI/UX specification for the SPO application suite, extracted from the DonorCRM frontend: brand palette and semantic light/dark tokens, typography scale, shape and elevation rules, component and layout conventions, accessibility requirements, copy-paste starter files (globals.css, Tailwind config, theme bootstrap, cn helper), and a list of known drifts not to replicate.
nodes.languageNotes: Leads with five non-negotiable rules (outlined CTAs, navy body text, bordered cards, 12px radius, generous section spacing) so the distinguishing choices survive even when the rest of the spec is skimmed.

nodes.name: 0002_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0003_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after `0003_add_audit_log`, recording the append-only `audit_log` table added for access, money and document events.

nodes.name: 0004_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after `0004_add_audit_log_filter_indexes`; the table set is unchanged and the difference is the new indexes supporting audit-log filtering.

nodes.name: 0005_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after `0005_add_property_chapter`, capturing the free-text `chapter` column added to `properties`.

nodes.name: 0006_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after `0006_drop_question_answers`, recording the removal of the unused walkthrough question-answer columns.

nodes.name: 0007_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after `0007_add_maintenance_schedules`, capturing the new `maintenance_schedules` table for preventive and safety maintenance.

nodes.name: 0008_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after `0008_add_residents`, capturing the `residents` table that records who lives in each house.

nodes.name: _journal.json
nodes.summary: Drizzle Kit's migration journal: the ordered index of all ten applied migrations, each entry pairing an index and timestamp with the descriptive migration tag. Renaming a generated migration file means updating its `tag` here to match.
nodes.languageNotes: The `tag` values are hand-edited after `npm run db:generate` so the journal reflects the descriptive migration filenames rather than Drizzle's random default names.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: The single HTML shell Vite builds the SPA from: sets the page title and description, preconnects to Google Fonts, loads the theme-init script before paint, and mounts React into #root via /src/main.tsx.
nodes.languageNotes: The theme script is an external file rather than inline specifically so the production Content Security Policy in server/security.ts can forbid inline scripts outright.

nodes.name: theme-init.js
nodes.summary: Render-blocking IIFE that reads the saved theme from localStorage (falling back to the device preference) and toggles the `dark` class before React paints, so the page never flashes the wrong theme.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately plain ES5-style script with try/catch around both localStorage and matchMedia, so private-browsing or an old engine degrades to following the device rather than throwing before first paint.

nodes.name: use-mobile.tsx
nodes.summary: Exposes the `useIsMobile` hook, which tracks whether the viewport is below the 768px breakpoint so components (notably the collapsible sidebar) can switch layout.

nodes.name: useIsMobile
nodes.summary: React hook that subscribes to a `(max-width: 767px)` media query and returns a boolean for the current viewport, cleaning up its listener on unmount.

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: The global stylesheet: Tailwind's base/components/utilities layers plus the SPO design tokens — HSL colour variables for light and dark, the 12px radius, elevation and typography defaults that every shadcn primitive reads through.
nodes.languageNotes: Colours are stored as bare HSL channel triplets in CSS custom properties so Tailwind's `<alpha-value>` syntax in tailwind.config.ts can compose opacity onto them.

nodes.name: drizzle.config.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle Kit configuration pointing the migration tooling at shared/schema.ts and the ./migrations output directory for Postgres; throws at load time if DATABASE_URL is missing.

nodes.name: a11y.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Accessibility gate: runs axe-core over the dashboard, properties, assets gallery, residents and finances pages and fails on any serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA violation.
nodes.languageNotes: Three SPO brand colours miss AA contrast by a hair (issue #35) and are tolerated by an explicit allowlist, so a genuinely new contrast regression still fails the gate rather than the whole check being disabled.

nodes.name: seriousViolations
nodes.summary: Runs an AxeBuilder scan tagged wcag2a/wcag2aa against the current page and returns only the serious and critical violations, with the known brand-contrast findings filtered out.

nodes.name: assets.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite for the Asset Tracking page: checks the fixed/movable tabs, that the list view is the default, that switching to the gallery renders asset tiles, and that the chosen view survives a reload.

nodes.name: auth.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite covering the signed-in and signed-out entry points: an admin session lands on the Dashboard with no login button, while a fresh cookie-less context gets the Landing page and a sign-in button.

nodes.name: dashboard.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite for the admin dashboard: each stat tile navigates to its section (properties, maintenance, contacts, assets) and the sidebar logo returns home.

nodes.name: finances.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite for the resident Finances page: the nav item opens it with the rent month picker and record control, and the Deposits tab reaches its add-deposit control.

nodes.name: global-setup.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright global setup that stands in for OIDC login: it upserts an admin and a resident test user with full permissions, mints signed session cookies directly into the sessions table, saves them as storage state, and writes a fixtures.json of real seeded IDs for the specs.
nodes.languageNotes: Works only because the harness knows SESSION_SECRET and can sign a connect.sid cookie the same way the server does — the application itself gains no test-only login path.

nodes.name: ensureUser
nodes.summary: Idempotently inserts or updates a test user row and grants every permission flag, so the admin and resident fixtures exist with a known role before any spec runs.

nodes.name: mintSession
nodes.summary: Writes a session row for the given user into the Postgres session store and returns the HMAC-signed cookie value that points at it, reproducing what a real OIDC login would leave behind.

nodes.name: saveStorageState
nodes.summary: Persists a signed session cookie as a Playwright storage-state JSON file so specs start already signed in as that user.

nodes.name: globalSetup
nodes.summary: Default-exported entry point: opens a pool, ensures both test users exist, gives the resident an owned maintenance request, saves admin and resident storage states, and writes fixtures.json with real property and asset IDs.

nodes.name: mobile.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite that runs only under the Pixel 5 project: asserts the dashboard has no horizontal overflow and that navigation lives behind the sidebar toggle at phone width.

nodes.name: properties.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite for the Properties page filters: verifies the region and chapter selects are present and that choosing a seeded chapter genuinely narrows the card list to that chapter.

nodes.name: resident.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite driving the app as a resident: the resident dashboard and submit action, a sidebar with no admin sections, their own request under My Requests, and a refusal when an admin URL is entered directly.
nodes.languageNotes: Overrides storageState per file with `test.use({ storageState: 'e2e/.auth/resident.json' })`, which is how a single suite swaps identity away from the default admin session.

nodes.name: residents.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite for the Residents roster: the nav item opens the page with its current/former tabs and add control, and seeded residents appear grouped by house with a headcount.

nodes.name: safety.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Playwright suite for the Safety & Upkeep page: opens it from the nav with its safety and preventive tabs, and applies the standard schedule template to a seeded house to confirm schedule cards and a compliance count appear.

nodes.name: playwright.config.ts

nodes.name: postcss.config.js
nodes.summary: Minimal PostCSS configuration wiring Tailwind and Autoprefixer into the Vite CSS pipeline.

nodes.name: baselineMigrations.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the migration baseline checker, run against the project's real migration files rather than fixtures because the original bug was a mismatch between what the check expected and what the actual migrations do.
nodes.languageNotes: Regression cover for a dead-end upgrade path: reading only CREATE TABLE meant a column dropped by a later migration was still expected present, so every real database failed the baseline check and then failed db:migrate too.

nodes.name: baseline-migrations.ts
nodes.summary: Backs `npm run db:baseline`: records migrations up to a given tag as already applied in Drizzle's __drizzle_migrations table, after verifying the live schema really matches what those migrations describe, so a database that predates migrations/ can join the migration history.
nodes.languageNotes: Migration identity is the SHA-256 of the whole .sql file, matching how Drizzle recognises a migration — any drift there would make Drizzle treat a recorded migration as new and try to run it again.

nodes.name: readJournal
nodes.summary: Loads and validates migrations/meta/_journal.json, failing with a clear message if the journal is missing or empty.

nodes.name: expectedSchema
nodes.summary: Replays the SQL of the given migration tags to derive the table and column set those migrations should leave behind, honouring later ALTER TABLE additions and drops rather than only CREATE TABLE.

nodes.name: tablesAddedAfter
nodes.summary: Returns the tables created by migrations beyond the baseline point, so their presence in the live database is not mistaken for unexpected drift.

nodes.name: compareSchema
nodes.summary: Diffs the expected schema against what the database actually contains and reports missing tables, missing columns and unexpected extras, ignoring tables a later migration legitimately added.

nodes.name: tagMatching
nodes.summary: Picks the migration tag whose expected schema best matches the live database, so the script can suggest the right baseline point when the user did not name one.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses the tag and --force arguments, reads the live schema from information_schema, verifies it matches the migrations being baselined, then inserts their hashes into __drizzle_migrations inside a transaction.

nodes.name: vitest.config.ts
